opportunities.title: Fix the front door and put a qualifying intake agent behind it
opportunities.problem: The firm has no working web front door. Every page I loaded hung on a full-screen percentage preloader with no content rendered (taxes page stuck at 9% at 1440px; home page at 32% at 500px; contacts page climbed 12% to 27% at 390px), the hero and nav 'Schedule an appointment' buttons are either a dead 404 or have no href, and the only form on the site is the header search box - so a nonprofit that found them through Google, a referral or their own Google Ads creative cannot read the offer, call from a phone, or request a consultation.
evidence: Full-screen percentage preloader never completes: taxes page at 9%, contacts page climbing 12% to 27% at 390px with no page content rendered (https://rakotygroup.com/contacts/)
Hero 'Schedule an appointment' links to https://rakotygroup.com/contacts-us/ which returns HTTP 404; nav and in-page instances have no href; /careers/ also 404s (https://rakotygroup.com/)
No contact form anywhere: Contact Form 7 and WPForms scripts load but zero form widgets render, so intake is phone, email or walk-in only (https://rakotygroup.com/contacts/)

Title is 'Rakoty - Nonprofit Accounting company' with no town; meta description still contains placeholder instruction text; JSON-LD is WebPage/Organization with no LocalBusiness/AccountingService, address or phone (https://rakotygroup.com/)

Paid demand is being generated against that dead end: pages rewritten Aug-Oct 2026 and a Google Ads creative 'Google-ads-Desktop-contact' uploaded 2026-10, with GTM-W5QWST8X installed (https://rakotygroup.com/page-sitemap.xml)

Live theme demo copy with fictitious staff ('Monica Black, chief communication officer') still published on /about-rakoty/, which is what a prospect evaluating credibility would land on (https://rakotygroup.com/about-rakoty/)

Triage.json corrections applied: the nav CTA target /contacts-us/ is a 404, and no contact form exists on any page checked - the earlier 'contact_form: true' note was wrong (https://rakotygroup.com/contacts-us/)
opportunities.agent_design: Two layers. (1) Front-door repair: remove or time-box the preloader, self-host and compress the Elementor/theme assets so first contentful paint is under ~2.5s on 4G, restore the real 'Schedule an appointment' path, put a short intake form (nonprofit vs small business, org name, fiscal year end, grant-funded y/n, 990 due date, current bookkeeping system) and a tap-to-call button on every page, and emit LocalBusiness/AccountingService JSON-LD with address, hours and phone so assistants and crawlers can read and route the business. (2) Intake agent on top: form, web and phone-voicemail submissions trigger an agent that enriches the org (990/ProPublica-style public filings, EIN-level basics), scores fit against the firm's nonprofit ICP and its $99/month volume tier, drafts the reply and the proposed call slots, and writes the record into a lightweight pipeline board. The agent sends nothing until a person approves the outbound reply; anything unusual (state-funded audit, multi-state payroll, IRS notice) is routed as an exception to a named Client Manager. The agent also logs every abandoned or unqualified enquiry so the firm can see what the ads are actually producing.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A Wix/WordPress plugin cannot fix a theme that never renders, and a chatbot widget bolted on top of a page that shows 27% is worse than nothing. The work spans performance diagnosis on a specific Elementor/Maxbizz build, structured-data and crawler legibility, form-to-CRM plumbing through GTM, and an agent that must read public filings to qualify a nonprofit enquiry - then hand off with human approval. It also needs someone accountable for the site not silently breaking again, which is the retainer layer.

impact_estimate.range: Unblocks 100% of current web demand (today 0 of an unknown number of visitors can read or act on the site) and, on conservative assumptions, recovers roughly 2-6 enquiries/month of which 1-2 convert - about $1,200-$7,000 in first-year recurring revenue at the firm's own published $99/month entry price, before counting any larger nonprofit engagement
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes the Google Ads and organic traffic is non-zero (ads creative uploaded Oct 2026, GTM installed) but that essentially all of it is lost today because no page renders and no CTA works; assumes 2-6 recoverable enquiries/month and a 25-50% close rate at the published $99/month tier. No sourced benchmark for accounting-firm inbound conversion was found, so no revenue beyond the firm's own published price is claimed; the value of no longer wasting paid clicks is real but unquantified because the ad budget is not public.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: preloader removed and Core Web Vitals/LCP measured before and after at 390px and 1440px; working 'Schedule an appointment' path with intake form and tap-to-call live on home, nonprofit, small-business, taxes and contacts pages; LocalBusiness/AccountingService schema validating in Google's test tool; one intake agent running on form submissions with approval-gated replies and a simple pipeline board; before/after screenshots of the phone-width site as the demo.

opportunities.title: Nonprofit document-chasing and deadline agent for close, audit and 990 season
opportunities.problem: The firm's published scope is a chain of recurring, deadline-bound document collections from client finance staff: monthly close by the 10th, grant budget-to-actual reporting monthly and quarterly, cost allocation across grants, annual audit leadership with state auditors, 990 preparation and the 1099/W-2 season - plus a named Client Manager also acting as bookkeeper or part-time CFO. Every one of those deadlines starts with someone at Rakoty emailing a client to ask, again, for a missing statement or approval.
evidence: Published deliverables: monthly close by the 10th, grant budget-to-actual by month and quarter, cost allocation across grants, W-2/1099/1096 runs, annual audit reports and 990 (https://rakotygroup.com/non-profit-2/)
Weekly vendor payment runs 'after approvals' and a named Client Manager as part-time CFO or full-time bookkeeper - a per-client manual approval queue (https://rakotygroup.com/non-profit-2/)

Nonprofit clients are remote and multi-state (Philadelphia, NYC foster care, 'we serve small organizations all over the nation'), so document collection is entirely by email rather than in person (https://rakotygroup.com/small-businesses/)

Reviews credit the firm specifically with rescuing backlogged books and billings - one client says they caught up to billings, another praises a seamless QuickBooks transition, i.e. document and data cleanup is already their differentiator (https://www.dosfinds.us/firms/rakoty-accountants)

Vendor-sponsored surveys of US accountants (self-reported, not independent cost measurements): 49% typically spend 1-2 days gathering information for a single engagement and 16% two weeks or more; average 9.3 hours a week on client communication (https://doxalio.com/blog/cost-of-chasing-client-documents-accounting-firms)

Field evidence on what AI-assisted workflows change: a Stanford working paper (not peer-reviewed) on 79 small and mid-sized firms reports a 7.5-day reduction in monthly close time and about 8.5% of accountant time reallocated away from routine data entry (https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/working-papers/human-ai-accounting-early-evidence-field)
opportunities.agent_design: A per-client document request list generated from the engagement type (monthly close pack, quarterly grant report, audit PBC list, 990 organizer, year-end 1099/W-2), held in the firm's own document store. Triggers: calendar dates (close by the 10th, filing deadlines, fiscal year end), and a nightly diff of what is still missing against QuickBooks/bank statement coverage and the grant budget-to-actual sheet. The agent sends a specific ask - the named document, period and amount, not 'send your documents' - chases on a fixed cadence, parses what arrives, files and renames it, updates the request list, and writes the budget-to-actual rollup for the Client Manager. Escalation rules keep it safe: unmatched or stale items, anything naming an IRS notice or a state auditor, and every grant-report submission go to a human queue with the agent's draft. Runs inside the firm's own tenancy with retention/deletion settings, no client tax data sent to an outside model provider without the firm's documented consent and contract.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This touches QuickBooks, bank statements, payroll, grant budgets and client PII under IRC Sec. 7216 and the FTC Safeguards Rule (tax preparers are 'financial institutions' requiring a written security program, MFA and service-provider oversight) - so it cannot be an off-the-shelf AI assistant with client files pasted in. It needs real systems integration, per-client state that survives months, reminder logic that does not annoy clients into complaining, and escalation that a licensed preparer can defend in an audit trail.

impact_estimate.range: Save roughly 10-25 staff hours per month across close and audit season, worth about $280-$700/month at the NJ bookkeeping-clerk median wage ($58,300/yr, about $28/hour) and $485-$1,210/month at the NJ accountant median ($100,830/yr, about $48/hour); call it $3,000-$12,000 a year of recovered capacity, plus a shorter close
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes a bench of preparers (directory listing says 11-50 employees, unverified) and roughly 1-3 hours of chasing per client per close cycle across a client book of a few dozen nonprofits; range widens if the firm is nearer 10 staff. Wage math is BLS May 2025 NJ medians divided by 2,080 hours and excludes payroll overhead, so it understates loaded cost. The Stanford working paper's 7.5-day close reduction is from one vendor's small and mid-sized firm clients and likely over-represents adopters, so it is used only as directional support, not applied to the hour range. The document-gathering survey figures are vendor-sponsored self-reports and are not used to price anything.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks on 3-5 volunteer nonprofit clients: one standardised request-list template per engagement type, agent-generated specific asks with a fixed chase cadence, automatic filing and renaming of returned documents, and a missing-items dashboard the Client Manager reads each morning; measured against last month's manual baseline of hours spent chasing and days-to-close, with before/after evidence from a single client's quarter.

opportunities.title: Grant, 990 and cost-allocation knowledge agent for client finance staff and Rakoty's own bench
opportunities.problem: Rakoty's moat is nonprofit compliance knowledge - grants management, cost allocation, audit leadership, 990 - and it already sells 'training and support' and 'technical support' as service lines. That expertise currently leaves the firm one question at a time, by email and phone, from client bookkeepers and executive directors who ask the same things every cycle; nothing is captured, so the same answer is retyped and the same client cannot self-serve.
evidence: Service list explicitly includes 'training and support', 'technical support', 'government grants management' and 'customized services' alongside accounting and 990 work (https://rakotygroup.com/)

The firm publishes its expertise as articles - IRS 990, cost allocation, accrual basis, partnership tax - through Sept 2025, i.e. the raw material for a knowledge base already exists in its own words (https://rakotygroup.com/blog/)
Client-facing role is 'dedicated Client Manager' acting as part-time CFO, which means a steady stream of client questions routed to one named person (https://rakotygroup.com/non-profit-2/)
Reviews praise responsiveness and grants/compliance knowledge, so speed of answer is part of what clients are paying for (https://www.dosfinds.us/firms/rakoty-accountants)

Task-type evidence: a generative-AI assistant rolled out to 5,179 support agents raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average and 34% for novices (Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond, published in QJE 2025) - adjacent structured knowledge work, not accounting-specific (https://academic.oup.com/qje/article/140/2/889/7990658)

Firm-side evidence: the same Stanford working paper (not peer-reviewed) reports a 55% increase in weekly client support volume at small and mid-sized firms using one AI accounting platform (https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/working-papers/human-ai-accounting-early-evidence-field)
opportunities.agent_design: A retrieval agent over documents the firm owns and controls: its own published articles, internal SOPs and close checklists, grant agreements and budget templates clients have shared, 990 instructions and Uniform Guidance excerpts, and the firm's own FAQ. Two front doors - a client-facing answer box inside the client portal that answers 'how do I code this restricted grant expense' or 'what do you need for my 990' with a citation to the exact source passage, and a staff-facing console where a preparer asks the same thing. Every answer shows its citations; anything below a confidence threshold, anything asking for a judgement (is this allowable, should we file an extension) and every tax position is refused and routed to the named Client Manager. Answers are logged so the firm can see which questions to turn into new articles and which clients need training. Deployed in the firm's own cloud tenant with 7216/FTC-compatible contracts, no client identifiers sent to a third-party model without documented consent.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A general chatbot will confidently invent a grant-allowability rule, and one wrong answer to a nonprofit finance director costs the firm the account - or worse, ends up in an audited grant report. Doing this correctly means controlled ingestion of the firm's documents, per-client permission boundaries so one client cannot see another's grant agreements, citation-enforced answers, refusal routing to a human, and logging that a reviewer can audit. That is retrieval engineering plus governance, not a subscription.

impact_estimate.range: Deflect or shorten roughly 3-8 hours a week of routine client and staff Q&A, worth about $75-$380/week ($300-$1,600/month) at NJ wage medians, and let the same bench absorb more of the $99/month volume tier without adding a hire
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes one named Client Manager per client and a repeating question load across roughly two dozen nonprofit clients; hour range is a conservative fraction of the survey-reported 9.3 hours/week of client communication, since only the routine, document-answerable share is addressed. Priced at the NJ bookkeeping-clerk median ($58,300/yr) for the client-facing share and the NJ accountant median ($100,830/yr) for the staff share, excluding overhead. The 14% and 55% productivity findings are from adjacent task types or one vendor's adopter-heavy client base, so they are used to justify the direction of the estimate, not to multiply it.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: ingest the firm's blog archive, close checklists and one client's grant agreements; a staff-facing console answering 990, cost-allocation and close-checklist questions with citations; a scored test set of 30 real past questions reviewed by a preparer for accuracy and refusal behaviour; a suggestion list of the top 10 questions to publish as client-facing articles; a permissions model demonstrated with two client document sets that cannot see each other.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (22/30): the front-door failure is directly observed and unusually severe - blank pages at 390px, a 404 'Schedule an appointment', no form anywhere, placeholder meta copy, fictitious staff names still live - on top of document-heavy recurring deliverables (close by the 10th, quarterly grant budget-to-actual, audit PBC lists, 990, 1099/W-2) that are all document chasing by another name. It is held below 25 because the internal labor pain is inferred from published scope, not observed. Fit (16/20): three of the three opportunities map cleanly onto G, A and C, and the confidentiality regime (IRC 7216, FTC Safeguards Rule) points to private/contracted deployment, which is a capability rather than a problem. Ability to pay (12/20): established practice with ~24 nonprofit logos, national and out-of-state clients, active paid marketing and a published $99/month product line, and a directory listing of 11-50 staff - but headcount, revenue and the owner are all unverified, and there is no named decision maker (the profile can only infer a principal called 'Bass' from reviews). Ease (12/15): the front-door fix is days, not weeks, needs no client data access, and a phone-width before/after screenshot is the entire sales conversation. Strategic (13/15): the same package - front door, document-chase agent, nonprofit knowledge agent - resells to any small practice in a dense niche; NJ NAICS 5412 has 4,396 establishments and Middlesex County 346, with high average pay, so there are hundreds of plausible buyers for the same build. No physical/edge (E) opportunity is proposed: there is no avenues.json in this folder and no physical operation to instrument - the firm's footprint is a single professional office suite with no fleet, kitchen, dock, inventory or shop floor, clients are served remotely or at client sites, and the only camera-shaped use (office security) would need a licensed NJ alarm contractor under N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2 while addressing none of the pain the evidence shows.

best_evidence_signal: The hero 'Schedule an appointment' CTA returns HTTP 404 and every page stalls on a full-screen preloader that never clears (9-32% at 390px, 500px and 1440px), so the firm is running Google Ads into a site no visitor can read, call from or submit a request on - https://rakotygroup.com/contacts/
